business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal jurisdiction; no sub-state tax carve-out; cantonal commercial register offices form the registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (statutory Swiss Civil Code, Code of Obligations, and Federal Acts; no common law precedent doctrine)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland – PRC Double Taxation Agreement (signed 25 September 2013, in force from 1 January 2015 for Swiss tax)
EFTA – China Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 July 2014)
Switzerland – US DTA as amended by the 2009 Protocol (in force 23 September 2011)
Switzerland – United Kingdom DTA (in force 9 December 2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997, as amended (2023 revision); Ordinance on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLO, SR 955.01); Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 628a (SR 220) (internal register of beneficial owners); Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis and Art. 305ter (SR 311.0); FINMA AML due-diligence circulars; SECO sanctions ordinances under the Embargo Act (SR 946.231).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Deed of incorporation and statutes (Errichtungsurkunde / Statuten) of the Aktiengesellschaft
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the Canton of the registered seat
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization under Art. 629 CO; Swiss-internal document, no apostille required for registration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and proof of residence of all founders and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing state authority (e.g., competent authority of the founders' states)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Switzerland and the PRC are both Contracting States to the 1961 Apostille Convention; apostille issued by the issuing state's competent authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial-ownership declaration (UBO register excerpt) for each direct or indirect owner holding at least 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille if executed outside Switzerland

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for subscription of nominal capital (CHF 100,000 minimum, CHF 50,000 payable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Depositary financial institution of the investors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Counter-certification by the issuing bank; apostille only if expressly required by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granted to the Swiss incorporation agent or counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for each power of attorney signed abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All founders, directors, and beneficial owners must be screened at onboarding and on a rolling 90-day cycle against the Swiss SECO sanctions ordinances, UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list (required for USD clearing through Stripe and any US correspondent banking), EU consolidated list, and FINMA-issued enforcement lists; PEP status (Art. 2a AMLA) triggers mandatory enhanced due diligence, identification of the source of funds, and senior-management approval; negative news and politically exposed family-member screening is required for this online retail business as a Low_Risk_Standard AML tier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch) and the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office portal, electronically integrated through EasyGov.swiss (Federal Council e-Government)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be expressed in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian, or Romansh). The legal-form suffix may appear only in the statutory forms: 'Aktiengesellschaft' / 'AG' (German), 'Société anonyme' / 'SA' (French), or 'Società anonima' / 'SA' (Italian). Foreign-alphabet transliteration (e.g., pinyin) is permissible as a coined root name but requires a Swiss-language legal-form suffix; the registry will reject names that are false, misleading, or contrary to public interest under Art. 950–952 CO and Art. 34 of the Commercial Register Ordinance (CRR, SR 221.411).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca (requires banking licence under Art. 1 Banking Act)
Trust / Treuhand (requires special trust licence and a true fiduciary structure)
Schweizer / Swiss / Suisse / Svizzero (unjustified use; only if Art. 33 CO conditions of being organized and managed in Switzerland are met)
Nationalbank / Banque Nationale (exclusive to the Swiss National Bank)
Licensed / Broker / Exchange (terms implying regulated financial activity under FINMA standards)
Any term violating Art. 950(2) CO by suggesting a business capacity or duration the company does not possess
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A preliminary name reservation expires after 90 days unless the Cantonal Commercial Register Office grants a single renewal of a further 90 days upon written motion filed before expiry. If the name is rejected: (a) request a formal refusal order (Verfügung) from the Commercial Register Office under Art. 36(2) CRR; (b) appeal within 10 days of service to the cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Commission; (c) further appeal to the Federal Administrative Court and ultimately the Federal Supreme Court under Art. 82ff. BGG; during the appeal, the registry may provisionally reserve the disputed name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partial – a pure mail-forwarding or unattended virtual office does not satisfy the statutory seat requirement (Art. 626 para 1 CO). The registered seat must be a real municipal address in Switzerland with physical desk space, reception, authorised mailbox access, and a person capable of receiving court and registry service. Serviced offices and registered-agent premises satisfying these conditions are acceptable for this unlicensed online furniture retail business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – for an unlicensed, low-risk e-commerce business the annual probability of an unannounced commercial-register confirmation visit is estimated at 2–5%; cantonal tax authorities may request proof of business substance only if turnover or loss thresholds trigger inquiry; no premise-inspection protocol applies unless local retail activity is found on site.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Art. 45 CRR and SHAB publication fee tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Office of Justice – Legalisation Section, Bern
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal Justice Office fee schedule and Hague Apostille Convention (1961)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per official translator tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the internal UBO register (Art. 628a CO) and shareholder title ledger

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP / sanctions / OFAC / UN / SECO baseline screening database (one-time licence and execution)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service, serviced seat, secretariat, and postal handling (three-month deposit)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Arts. 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft), especially Arts. 626–636 (formation and capitalization); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Arts. 17–19 and 33–39; Federal Ordinance on Commercial Register Fees (GebV-HReg), Art. 7; Federal Act on the Adaptation of Company Law of 19 June 2020 (in force since 1 January 2023).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) at the seat canton, operated under the supervisory oversight of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office, Federal Office of Justice, Bern; filings performed via the electronic eGR portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Public Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungserklärung / acte constitutif) containing the Articles of Association (Statuten / statuts) and the Declaration of Incorporation, submitted as a registration application (Anmeldung) through the eGR platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital is CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal amount of each subscribed share (aggregate floor of CHF 50,000) must be paid in cash before registration into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) opened at a Swiss bank in the name of the company in formation; if non-cash contributions (Sacheinlagen) are used, a sworn statutory audit confirmation of asset valuation is mandatory. At least one representative with authorized signatory power must be resident in Switzerland.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription and payment of the initial share capital having been verified, the Board of Directors adopts the Registered Office at [address], Zürich, Switzerland, and the Company's statutory organization. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name A] is appointed Chairman, [Name B] is appointed Delegate of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, and [Name C] is appointed Secretary, each to serve until the first Annual General Meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairman and the CEO are granted individual signatory authority, audit powers are waived pursuant to Art. 727a OR, and the Swiss Commercial Register application, bank account opening, and all corporate formalities are hereby ratified and authorized.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Notarization, and Execution of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Öffentlicher Notar / Notaire) in the canton of the registered office, with prior non-binding name availability check by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a notary to draft the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association; all founding shareholders must physically attend the notarial session, subscribe shares, adopt the articles, elect the first Board of Directors, and either appoint the statutory auditor or execute a unanimous shareholder opt-out resolution under Art. 727a OR. The notary then authenticates the deed and transmits it electronically to the Commercial Register Office via the eGR system.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (German or French)
Passport or ID copies of all founding shareholders
Certificate of name availability from the Commercial Register Office
Share subscription list with designation of contribution types
Auditor appointment confirmation or unanimous opt-out declaration
Acceptance statements of the first Board members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the Commercial Register Office flags name conflicts, corporate purpose, or capital clauses, the founders execute a supplementary notarial deed amending the articles; the registration clock restarts upon resubmission through the eGR portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Escrow Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank (e.g., UBS, Zürcher Kantonalbank, or another bank supervised by FINMA) operating the Sperrkonto in the name of the company in formation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized deed and provisional Commercial Register documentation to the bank; the bank opens a blocked capital deposit account, verifies beneficial ownership under anti-money laundering rules (CDB 2020), and receives the cash payment of at least CHF 50,000. The bank issues an irrevocable written confirmation (Freigabebestätigung) that the funds are at the company's disposal and will be released only upon production of the Commercial Register excerpt.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized deed of incorporation
Passport copies of authorized signatories
Beneficial owner and source-of-funds declarations
Bank's standard account opening forms
Provisional company data sheet from the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions source of funds or beneficial ownership, provide corroborating evidence (bank statements, contracts, payroll records); if the account is refused, select a second licensed Swiss bank and withdraw the application; the Commercial Register application remains unaffected because the bank confirmation is submitted directly by the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board of Directors Meeting and Adoption of Organizational Regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's registered office in Switzerland; board meeting minuted by the appointed Secretary, with legal verification by the board chairman.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to verify capitalization, adopt the organizational regulations (Organisationsreglement), assign signature powers (individual, collective of two, or power of attorney), open the corporate governing minute book and share ledger, and formally ratify the Commercial Register application and post-registration actions caused by management.
required_dossiers: Draft minutes of the first board meeting
Organizational regulations with delegation of management powers
List of authorized signatories with signature specimens
Share register (Aktienbuch) opening page
Board resolutions ratifying the registered office and bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any board member cannot physically attend, valid video conference participation is permitted by the articles; if a quorum fails, the meeting is reconvened within 48 hours; missing signatures are collected by circulation and appended to the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Registration with the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) at the registered office seat, operating the federal eGR electronic filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or authorized representative submits the complete registration application through eGR, attaching the notarized deed, bank confirmation, board documents, and auditor waiver. The Commercial Register Examiner verifies legal compliance, the registered office address, and effective management structure; upon approval, the company acquires legal personality and the register office issues an official excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) and publishes the registration in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation and articles of association
Bank's blocked account confirmation certifying paid-up capital
Board meeting minutes and organizational regulations
Acceptance declarations of directors and authorized signatories
Declaration identifying the registered office address (not a mere P.O. Box)
Auditor opt-out unanimous resolution or auditor appointment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the register issues a query (Zwischenverfügung), the deficiencies must be cured by supplementary declarations or documents within the stated deadline, usually 30–60 days; if registration is refused, the applicant may appeal the negative decree to the cantonal supervisory authority within 30 days and thereafter to the Swiss Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht); the notary coordinates submission of the corrected dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Formalities: Tax, Social Security, and Release of Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Cantonal Tax Administration, Cantonal AHV Compensation Office (SVA/Ausgleichskasse), and Suva accident insurance; the Swiss bank releases the Sperrkonto upon presentation of the Commercial Register excerpt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After legal personality is obtained, the company registers for VAT under Art. 10 of the Swiss VAT Act (if taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000), registers employees with the compensation fund for old-age and survivors' insurance (AHV/AVS) within 60 days retroactively, obtains employer accident insurance coverage with Suva or a private insurer, and submits the Commercial Register excerpt to the bank for immediate release of the paid-up capital. The federal VAT registration is performed online via the ESTV portal.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug)
VAT liquidation form and company data sheet (via ESTV portal)
AHV registration form with employee roster
Suva or private accident insurance policy confirmation
Bank account release instruction together with the excerpt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or AHV registrations are delayed, late registration penalties are minimized by filing retroactively with a just-cause statement; classification disputes concerning VAT status are resolved by a corrective filing to the cantonal VAT office with a right of objection within 30 days; any bank release delay is cured by obtaining a duplicate certified excerpt from the Commercial Register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Labor Inspectorate (Kantonales Arbeitsinspektorat) under the federal Labor Act (Arbeitsgesetz, ArG) and the Cantonal Building and Trade Police (Gewerbepolizei / Police du commerce), together with the Cantonal Fire Insurance Authority (Gebäudeversicherung); no sector-specific commercial license is required for online retail of furniture, but physical warehouse operations are subject to mandatory workplace and building permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Workplace Operating Permit (Betriebsbewilligung) under Art. 7 of the Swiss Labor Act and Art. 74 of Ordinance 1 to the Labor Act (ArGV 1), issued for the distribution and storage facility, coupled with a building use permit (Gebäudenutzungsbewilligung) for the oversized furniture warehouse from the cantonal building authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Cantonal Environmental Protection Office (Kantonales Amt für Umwelt) in coordination with the Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU/FOEN), applying the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/EIE) and cantonal environmental implementation acts.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration and screening (Vorprüfung) under Annex 1 UVPV: mandatory preliminary EIA screening if the warehouse or logistics project involves a gross floor area exceeding 20,000 m² or parking facilities above 300 spaces; for a standard oversized furniture distribution warehouse below these thresholds, the project is exempt from a full EIA report, subject solely to conditions imposed in the building permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: compliance with Annex 3.2 of the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV) for indirect discharge of sanitary and cleaning waters, with grease separators if applicable. Emissions: compliance with the Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV) limits for VOCs and particulate matter, including solvent balance records for any coating or finishing activities. Waste: compliance with the Ordinance on Waste Management (VVEA) requiring separated disposal of cardboard, wood, foams, and packaging waste, with proof of disposal by an authorized waste carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification obtained from the Cantonal Fire Insurance Authority (Gebäudeversicherung) and municipal fire police confirming compliance with VKF/AEAI fire protection standards, including emergency exits, extinguishing equipment, and storage height limits; structural load clearance evidenced by the approved structural engineering report and building permit; occupational safety clearance issued by the Cantonal Labor Inspectorate after inspection confirming compliance with ArGV 1 (workplace dimensions, lighting, ventilation, explosion protection, forklift traffic routes) and Suva safety directives for manual handling of oversized furniture, plus a certificate of no workplace health hazards per the federal labor law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Main VAT Division (Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer); official portal www.estv.admin.ch; secure e-filing and UID application portal via the ESTV QuickForm Suite and SWISS VAT web services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Swiss-incorporated Aktiengesellschaft (AG) must obtain a Swiss Business Identification Number (UID, format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) from the ESTV Central UID Register by filing the UID registration application (Formular UID 1) or through the online e-filing channel. Where annual worldwide taxable turnover reaches or exceeds CHF 100,000, the AG must simultaneously file an initial VAT registration (Formulare 201/202 or eServices) naming its Swiss statutory seat and Swiss-resident director as the local nexus; the UID number then serves as the VAT identification number (MWST-Nummer). A foreign beneficial owner may hold 100% of shares, no local residency or license is required for ISIC 4791 online retail, and the FTA issues the UID within approximately 2 to 4 weeks after submission. Foreign e-commerce sellers without Swiss establishment must register in the simplified non-established taxpayer procedure (Art. 65 MWSTG) if Swiss taxable turnover exceeds the threshold; as of 1 January 2025, marketplace platforms facilitating supplies by such sellers are jointly and severally liable for the underlying Swiss VAT under the new deemed-supplier rules (Art. 20a et seq. MWSTG).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation | Territorial_Scope: The AG is a resident corporation subject to unlimited tax liability (unbeschränkte Steuerpflicht) on worldwide profits, with profits attributable to foreign permanent establishments and foreign immovable property exempted under the exemption method. Federal corporate income tax applies at a flat rate of 8.5% on taxable profit (effective approximately 7.8% pre-tax); cantonal and communal profit taxes add a combined effective burden of roughly 11.9% in Zug to approximately 18-21% in Zurich and Geneva. No tax-exempt-zone regime applies in Switzerland; no pass-through eligibility exists for an AG.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a check-the-box system; the AG may mitigate double taxation only through statutory elections such as the participation exemption (Beteiligungsabzug) for qualifying dividends and capital gains, the deemed-capital-debt (Swiss safe interest) thin-capitalization rules, and the notional interest deduction regime election in certain cantons. For VAT, the AG may elect (i) the simplified tax-rate method (Art. 64 MWSTG) if taxable turnover is below CHF 5 million, (ii) voluntary registration even below the CHF 100,000 threshold (Art. 11 MWSTG), and (iii) monthly, quarterly, or semi-annual filing cycles. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognised; BEPS-compliant substantive arm's-length treatment is mandatory.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer MWST / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée TVA) as governed by the Federal Act on Value Added Tax (MWSTG) of 12 June 2009, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in annual worldwide taxable turnover (Art. 10 para. 1 MWSTG). Once the threshold is met, registration is compulsory from the point when the turnover has exceeded the amount; non-established foreign suppliers of goods in Switzerland are assessed on their Swiss-only taxable supplies, and marketplace platform operators are jointly liable for a non-established seller's VAT under Art. 20e MWSTG from 1 January 2025. Reduced rates: 2.6% for groceries, books, medicines, and certain essential goods; 3.8% for accommodation services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory central tax-stamping, or API-based clearance system (e.g., Italy's SDI) is in force in Switzerland as of the knowledge cutoff. The Confederation is the reference user of e-invoicing: invoices to the Swiss Federal Administration must be transmitted electronically in a structured format (XML, ZUGFeRD/facture-x, or the Swiss eBill standard) using the Swiss QR-Invoice payment part. The general statutory invoice content requirements of Art. 26 MWSTG (issuer, recipient, date, goods/services, consideration, VAT rate) remain the binding baseline for B2B and B2C documentation. The Federal Council has committed to a phased mandatory e-invoicing roadmap (public consultation and B2B mandate expected around 2027-2028), but until that is enacted e-invoicing among private parties is voluntary.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods from Swiss customs territory is tax-exempt (zero-rated) with full input VAT deduction in accordance with Art. 23 para. 1 MWSTG. For the ISIC 4791 online sale of oversized furniture and home decor, the following cumulative conditions must be satisfied: (i) the supplier or a third party physically transports the goods out of Switzerland to a foreign destination; (ii) the export is proven by an official customs export declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung) issued through the e-dec/E-Zoll process; (iii) the recipient is established or has its residence abroad, and the goods are effectively used abroad; and (iv) proof of export is obtained and retained prior to the filing deadline of the relevant assessment period. Related services (Art. 23 para. 2 MWSTG), including freight, assembly, and installation of exported furniture, are also zero-rated provided they directly benefit the overseas consignee. For EU-bound deliveries, proof may be substantiated by the Swiss export declaration plus EU customs transit documents (NCTS/ECS evidence); for online low-value consignments, the seller must additionally observe the distance-selling thresholds and import VAT rules in the destination jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung / export bordereau) generated through the Swiss e-dec-E-Zoll system, evidencing the outward customs treatment and exit validation
Commercial invoice and international sales contract (order confirmation) showing the foreign consignee, goods description, Incoterms (DAP/DDP), and consideration in CHF or foreign currency
Bill of Lading or CMR freight waybill / airway bill confirming physical cross-border carriage and the consignee's receipt of the oversized furniture

Inward remittance and settlement records (bank debit/credit advice, SWIFT MT103) demonstrating payment from the foreign buyer; Swiss VAT law does not statutorily require an 'Inward Remittance Certificate' as a strict condition of zero-rating, but the ESTV expects a transactional payment trail to counter fraud
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV applies thorough proof-of-export audits (Belegnachweisprüfung) and requires the customs declaration numbers to be listed in the VAT return annex. If the export documentation is missing or the goods are not physically exited, the ESTV retroactively classifies the supply as domestic, reassesses VAT at 8.1% on the full gross invoice amount, and charges default interest at 4.5% per annum plus late-payment penalties (Art. 82 and Art. 87 MWSTG). Simple procedural infringements are punishable by a fine of up to CHF 30,000 (Art. 98 MWSTG). Intentional or grossly negligent tax evasion (Abgabebetrug, Art. 99 MWSTG) triggers imprisonment of up to 5 years or a substantial monetary penalty, with the ordinary 10-year reassessment limitation period applicable to fraudulent zero-rating claims (Art. 45 para. 1 MWSTG); directors and the responsible finance officers are jointly and severally liable, and the tax administration may suspend export zero-rating privileges and demand a security deposit before clearing further shipments. The 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation convention referenced in this dossier is a standard commercial treasury benchmark, not a statutory Swiss VAT condition of export zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera), acting under the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA; SR 941.10) and within the FINMA-supervised banking framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland grants full de jure and de facto convertibility on both current and capital account: the Swiss franc (CHF) floats freely, no exchange-control licensing, repatriation quotas, or minimum holding periods apply to inbound or outbound investment. Profit remittance from a Swiss AG (dividends, interest, royalties, liquidation proceeds) is legally unrestricted, subject only to the 35% statutory withholding tax on dividends, which may be reduced or refunded under an applicable double taxation treaty if the beneficial owner meets the treaty ownership threshold (usually 10% or higher) and the distributing entity has economic substance under the Aeschmann/Etat-Major practice. No SNB authorisation is required for equity injections, intercompany loans, or treasury sweeps; banks only file balance-of-payments statistics for cross-border client transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender regime exists in Switzerland: there is no mandated timeline for repatriation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to convert export receipts into CHF. E-commerce proceeds in USD, EUR, or other currencies may be retained offshore or onshore indefinitely and converted at the merchant's discretion. The only compliance duties are SNB balance-of-payments statistical reporting by banks for cross-border payments above CHF 100,000 per reporting period and federal customs export declarations for physical furniture shipments; neither involves FX conversion requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: UBS Switzerland AG (corporate coverage in Zug and Zurich)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency CHF/EUR/USD) with dedicated Capital Escrow Account (Gruendungskonto) if the AG is within 12 months of formation
Operational Account (CHF with EUR/USD sub-accounts via SIC/euroSIC and correspondent clearing); Capital Escrow Account for new formations
Operational Account (CHF; foreign currency via SIC/euroSIC and SWIFT correspondents)
Operational Account (multi-currency with acquirer-integrated settlement products)
Private Banking Custody and Wealth Management Account (asset-backed treasury, not suited for high-frequency e-commerce settlement)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for principal bank status, Moderate as a collection sub-rail. An offshore digital EMI (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) without FINMA authorisation cannot serve as the primary settlement bank of a Swiss AG because the provision of payment accounts and payment services to Swiss clients is reserved for institutions licensed under the Banking Act, FinIA, and the FinTech licence regime (public deposits up to CHF 100 million without interest). Unlicensed EMIs may be used only as pass-through collection accounts (e.g., for US ACH or EU card receipts) with mandatory daily sweeps to the FINMA-supervised primary account. Recommended architecture: UBS or ZKB for payroll, VAT, dividend, and supplier payments; a FINMA-licensed fintech (YAPEAL, Bank Cler, Swissquote/Yuh) for high-frequency acquirer settlement; and a US ACH-capable correspondent account for Affirm BNPL USD payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one director or authorised signatory must appear physically before the onboarding desk of UBS, ZKB, or any cantonal or private bank; the original passport and proof of residential address are verified in person, and the compliance interview covers Form A/B UBO declarations (AMLA and FINMA Circular 2016/07), the source of funds for the minimum CHF 100,000 share capital (CHF 50,000 paid-in), and the e-commerce settlement model. Remote opening is not accepted for AG corporate structures at major banks; only FINMA-licensed digital banks (YAPEAL, Bank Cler) permit video-based onboarding, with lower transaction limits. A non-resident director may either travel to Switzerland or appoint a Swiss-resident deputy director holding signature rights; otherwise a notarised power of attorney must be deposited with the commercial register and accepted by the bank on a case-by-case basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership of the AG, particularly registered shares held by a non-resident holding company or any reference to pre-2019 bearer shares.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholders' register (Aktienbuch), current Handelsregisterauszug, Form A/B UBO declarations for every natural person holding 25% or more, group structure chart showing the ultimate beneficial owners, passport copies of all UBOs, and a board resolution certifying the absence of bearer shares following the 2019 dematerialisation reform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency aggregated e-commerce receivables from Stripe and Affirm BNPL that cannot be mapped to discrete retail sales of oversized furniture.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS 4.0 attestation of compliance, executed Stripe and Affirm merchant agreements, payout settlement reports with transaction-level identifiers, merchant category code (MCC) mapping, sample consumer orders with delivery addresses, and a transaction-flow diagram from card network to Stripe/Affirm to the bank account accepted by the compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds gap for the initial CHF 100,000 share capital deposit or a subsequent capital injection from a foreign parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 statements of the subscribing shareholder, signed equity subscription or loan agreement, notary confirmation of capital deposit release, Handelsregisterauszug and SHAB publication proof, and board minutes approving the formation or capital increase.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to high-risk furniture manufacturing jurisdictions (e.g., Vietnam, China, Poland, Turkey) with incomplete documentation and sanctions-list hits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supply contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading or CMR waybills, freight-forwarder agreements, supplier VAT or tax registration certificates, and counterparty due-diligence questionnaires with OFAC/EU/SECO sanctions screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Volatile cash-flow pattern from BNPL chargebacks and buyer refunds creating an apparent layering or third-party-beneficiary structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Affirm merchant agreement with underwriting terms, monthly chargeback-ratio report (target below 1%), refund policy and dispute-resolution SOP, treasury policy segregating consumer receivables from supplier payables, and interim financial statements demonstrating gross-margin consistency.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route all equity injections as SWIFT MT103/MT202 to the UBS or ZKB account: CHF clears via SIC, EUR via euroSIC/SEPA Instant, USD via CHIPS or Fedwire through the bank's US correspondent. Use purpose code 'Capital investment / equity contribution' or 'Intercompany loan' with reference to the notarised share subscription and loan agreement; no SNB approval is required, but the receiving bank must have complete underlying documentation for its balance-of-payments statistics and AML file. Verification protocol: match the incoming MT103 to the shareholders' ledger, deposit to a capital escrow sub-account if the AG is still in formation or credit directly to the operational account, and record a paid-in capital entry supported by board minutes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settle supplier payables by SWIFT MT103 for amounts below the LC threshold and by MT700/MT710 documentary letters of credit under UCP 600 for significant oversized-furniture purchases (typically above CHF 50,000). Standard commercial terms are 20-30% advance via MT103 and 70-80% against bill-of-lading presentation under a sight or 30/60-day usance LC. Use SWIFT gpi for end-to-end tracking and same-day value; USD clearing through a US correspondent is subject to OFAC sanctions screening and the correspondent bank's AML jurisdiction, and no US currency-transport reporting (CMIR) applies to electronic wires. Freight, customs duties, and import VAT are settled via SEPA Direct Debit or TPAY/TAXPORT-linked channels, and EUR disbursements should be offset against EUR e-commerce receivables to reduce FX exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, EUR/CHF) with tenors from one week to 12 months under an ISDA Master Agreement or Swiss Master Forward Contract; no SNB prior authorisation required.
European-style vanilla FX options (purchased or written) for contingent cash flows such as Affirm BNPL settlement timing, offered by licensed Swiss banks and their offshore branches.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS/MTM) to convert long-term USD/EUR e-commerce receivables into CHF operating liquidity or to hedge shareholder loans, governed by ISDA 2002 with standard CSA collateral terms.
FX spot and tomorrow-next swaps for daily sweeps between USD/EUR collection accounts and the CHF operating account to optimise working-capital netting.

NDFs (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF) are permissible only where the offshore counterparty cannot settle in CHF; given full Swiss franc convertibility, onshore deliverable forwards are the standard instrument for Swiss-resident entities, and NDFs are reserved for hedging an offshore parent's bridge financing or jurisdictions with restricted convertibility.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and audit report (Jahresrechnung und Revisionsbericht)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register of the canton of registered office (Handelsregister) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date, i.e. by 30 June for a 31 December fiscal year end; the shareholders' approval meeting must be held within the same period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry compliance order; administrative fines up to CHF 5,000; persistent non-compliance may lead to penalty proceedings and ultimately court-ordered dissolution/strike-off; directors face personal liability and criminal sanctions under Art. 325bis Swiss Criminal Code

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal, cantonal and municipal corporate income tax return (Steuererklärung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) for the registered canton; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) via the cantonal assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due by 31 March of the year following the tax period; extension to 30 June available on written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at approximately 3–4% per annum; late-filing fine up to CHF 5,000; estimated assessment by the tax authority; possible criminal tax penalty for willful non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT returns (quarterly declarations and annual reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV), Swiss VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly returns within 60 days after the calendar quarter; annual reconciliation for exempt and annual-filing taxpayers due within 60 days after the fiscal year end, generally by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 3–4% per annum; tax penalty up to CHF 8,000 or up to three times the tax evaded in willful cases; criminal prosecution for repeated violation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting minutes and shareholder resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Recorded in the company minute book; filed with public authorities only upon specific request or in the event of resolutions requiring commercial register amendment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within six months of the end of the fiscal year; minutes must be signed and retained immediately after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene may be remedied by court order at a shareholder's request; directors are liable for damages and may be fined under corporate criminal provisions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Register of Beneficial Owners (Register der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten) annual plausibility confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal register maintained at the registered office; accessible to prosecuting authorities, FINMA and cantonal enforcement offices; no public filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing update upon any share transfer or control change; annual confirmation of accuracy by the board of directors at the time of approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of Art. 697l of the Swiss Code of Obligations can lead to enforcement orders and fines up to CHF 10,000; false or incomplete entries carry criminal liability

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary mandatory audit is required if the company exceeds any two of the following thresholds for two consecutive years: balance sheet total CHF 20 million, turnover CHF 40 million, and 250 full-time employees. Companies below these thresholds may elect a limited review or, if eligible and opted-out by all shareholders, may exempt themselves from audit entirely.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) accounting provisions; local GAAP is predominantly Swiss GAAP FER (Fachempfehlung zur Rechnungslegung); IFRS is permitted and commonly used for internationally active or market-oriented companies; US GAAP is also accepted for certain consolidated financial reports

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no public UBO register. The AG must keep an internal register of beneficial owners under Art. 697l of the Swiss Code of Obligations, recording every natural person who holds more than 25% of shares or voting rights or who controls the company. The board must update this register on any transfer of shares and confirm its accuracy annually. Financial intermediaries conducting AML checks require such confirmation at least annually.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (Register der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten)
Accounting books, vouchers and business correspondence

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200–3,000 per year (CHF 1,000–2,700) for registered office services and resident company secretary or fiduciary agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if audit opt-out applies; USD 3,000–8,000 for a limited review; USD 8,000–25,000 for a full statutory audit of a medium-sized AG

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal direct tax on profits: 8.5% (effective 7.83% before tax); cantonal/communal rates vary from 11.9% (Zug) to 21% (Geneva) combined.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent box (max. 90% of IP income exempt at cantonal level), R&D super-deduction 150%, notional interest deduction (optional, cantonal), participation relief for dividends >10%, progressive levels; preferential holding/mixed statuses abolished as of 1 Jan 2020.
